judged_text: Salesforce's refresh never routes through the sync endpoint, but parseRefreshTokenResponse still switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever the sharing env vars are set, stripping the Salesforce response down to access_token before it is persisted. The credential update stores {access_token, refresh_token} — instance_url, id, signature, issued_at are destroyed; on the next service construction the jsforce Connection is built without instanceUrl and every Salesforce API call fails, corrupting Salesforce credentials even though Salesforce was never part of the credential-sync flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the Salesforce refresh flow always fetches directly from Salesforce (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and then parses via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`. However `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), regardless of whether the response actually came from the sync endpoint. That means when the sharing env vars + sync endpoint are configured, Salesforce’s full token response will be parsed/normalized by the minimum schema rather than `salesforceTokenSchema`, and the subsequent credential update (`data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`) can drop Salesforce-specific fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, `issued_at` that `salesforceTokenSchema` expects to preserve. This is consistent with corrupting stored Salesforce credentials even though Salesforce is not routed through `refreshOAuthTokens`/the sync endpoint in this diff.
